subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@acme.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Sara / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of pain points you called out:
- High 95th-percentile latency for chat responses across bursts, especially for long context sessions (customer support flows).
- Cost volatility when traffic spikes, and lack of predictable throughput for batch scoring use cases.
- Need for higher relevance in search results — current semantic search has noisy hits and you'd like a reranking step.
- Security/compliance checkpoints: SOC2 evidence and VPC/private networking are required for procurement.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Validate that Redwood can meet 95th pct latency targets (<400ms for short chat flows) with streaming responses.
2) Integrate Redwood SDK for function calling + structured outputs to automate ticket creation (avoid post-processing).
3) Prototype embeddings + reranker for the support KB and measure NDCG uplift.
4) Complete security questionnaire and get Dedicated or Private deployment options scoped for procurement.

Integration / product fit notes (technical):
- SDK: Our client SDK now supports function/tool calling primitives and deterministic structured output schemas (JSON Schema enforcement) — this will let you map model output directly into your ticket payloads.
- Streaming: Redwood offers chunked streaming responses and incremental function call payloads so you can display progressive answers in your UI (reduces perceived latency).
- Embeddings & Reranking: We recommend generating 1536-d embeddings (quantized) for initial retrieval, then a 2-stage reranker using a smaller cross-encoder. We can run the reranker in Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
- Fallbacks: We can route to a cheaper quantized variant on bursts and automatically fall back to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Attachments I dropped: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (SDK examples + sample function schemas). I've also attached a Mutual Action Plan workbook (RWF-Acme-MAP-20270518.xlsx) with milestones.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule 90-min technical deep-dive with your engineering + security (suggest Wed 5/19 or Thu 5/20). Link: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/tech-deep-dive?cid=rwf-acme-2027
- We’ll ship a small integration sample (SDK + function schema + streaming demo) that you can run against a redwood sandbox.
- Rishi (cc) will follow up with a preliminary pricing/commit recommendation for Dedicated capacity.
- You share your security questionnaire; we’ll assign an SOC2 contact and provide evidence.

If that all looks right, I’ll get the MAP updated and send an invite for the tech deep-dive.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-guide.pdf (15 pages) — SDK examples, streaming & function-calling snippets
- RWF-Acme-MAP-20270518.xlsx (Mutual Action Plan workbook)

From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches our notes. A few confirmations/questions from our side:

- Timeline: we are targeting a pilot with ~3 services in production by end of Q3. Procurement + security review needs to start this month.
- Security: please send the SOC2 contact and the artifact list (retention, audit logs, key management). We need the evidence for our security review.
- Tech deep-dive: Wed 5/19 10–11:30 PT works for our eng + security. Please lock that slot.
- Reranking: we want to understand latency impact of the 2-stage approach. Can the reranker run on the same Dedicated pool?

Also tagging our DevOps folks (devops@acme.com) — they’ll bring infra constraints (VPC peering, egress rules).

Sara Wong
Head of Product, Platform
Acme Cloud
sara.wong@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@acme.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Perfect — I locked the 5/19 10:00–11:30 PT slot and invited your team.

Quick answers:
- SOC2 / artifacts: attaching a checklist in the MAP and I’ll connect you to our security lead (privsec@redwood.com) during the deep-dive.
- Reranker latency: yes — you can colocate the cross-encoder reranker on Dedicated capacity; typical latency for a 2000-doc rerank is ~45–120ms per query depending on model/sequence length. We’ll include test vectors in the sandbox.
- Sandbox & sample: we’ll push an SDK sample that demonstrates function calling with a structured schema (ticket.create) and streaming response handling. Example snippet included in the attached PDF.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan milestones (from the MAP):
1) Week 1: Security kickoff + questionnaire completed
2) Week 2: Sandbox access + basic SDK demo integrated by Acme engs
3) Week 4: Reranker prototype + evaluation (NDCG)
4) Week 8: Pilot in 3 services + procurement decision (Dedicated vs Private)

I attached the MAP workbook and integration guide again. If you want, we can also do a short internal session with your data science team to instrument evaluation metrics (NDCG, precision@k).

Thanks — see you on 5/19.

Marissa

Marissa — quick internal note after the call and alignment thread.

- Pricing: for a pilot profile (burst-friendly, small reranker footprint), propose a 3-month trial at a blended rate reflecting 25% off list for committed Dedicated pool of 4 vGPU-equivalent nodes. We’ll have an alternate quote for Private (on-prem) once security scoping is done.
- Sales motions: I recommend we prepare a short one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Acme (latency, cost, security tradeoffs).
- Action: I’ll draft the pricing sheet and attach to the MAP by EOD Wed.
